focus: Adversarial audit of the So Min-ho investigation committee's changing composition, plus stronger election/person provenance for investigator nodes

material_findings.finding: A contemporaneous Seoul Shinmun report dated 1952-04-27 says the National Assembly Interior Committee initially planned a five-member Suncheon investigation team: Jo Sun, Yu Hong, Lee Seok-gi, Kim Jeong-gi and Choi Ju-il.

The archival catalog for Investigation Report No.1 dated 1952-05-09 instead names six special investigators: Yu Hong, Kim Gwang-jun, Jo Sun, Kim Jeong-gi, Jo Jeong-hun and Lee Seok-gi. Choi Ju-il is absent, while Kim Gwang-jun and Jo Jeong-hun appear.

The five-person April 27 press list and six-person May 9 report list must not be flattened into one committee membership fact. The safest current model is preliminary/planned delegation versus later report-signing special investigation committee, pending the Assembly appointment resolution and original report signatures.

Choi Ju-il is independently anchored as a legislator associated with Gimje and appears in a December 1952 National Assembly investigation context. This makes him a legitimate politician-node candidate rather than a likely OCR/name error.

A 1948 UNTCOK candidate-list document also indexes Choi Ju-il, providing a pre-1952 political trace, but the exact 1948 constituency/result must be extracted before treating it as an elected-office role.

The Central Election Commission compilation preserved by NIHK gives Kim Gwang-jun as the 1950 Ulchin winner, age 36, lawyer, independent, with 15,697 votes; Jo Jeong-hun as the Namwon winner, age 36, farmer, independent, with 17,022 votes.

The same election-source family plus contemporary election reporting supplies Hanja/name anchors for Jo Sun 趙淳, Jo Jeong-hun 趙定勳, Kim Gwang-jun 金光俊, Kim Jeong-gi 金正基 and Lee Seok-gi 李錫基, reducing modern-namesake contamination risk.
NIHK's person registry preserves Lee Seok-gi's birth conflict as 1907 versus 1908-01-02; this remains a provenance conflict, not a field to normalize silently.

NIHK's person registry gives Kim Jeong-gi as 金正基, born 1893, and records service as Suncheon county head, Mokpo mayor/buyeon, second-Assembly member and investigator in the National Defense Corps, Chosun Textile and So Min-ho cases.

FRUS document 135 describes the Assembly's May 14 action under Constitution Article 49, while the NIHK constitutional-history synthesis cites the exact Korean stenographic target as the 12th regular session record No.57 dated 1952-05-14. This narrows the next retrieval target without substituting the synthesis for the stenographic original.

adversarial_checks: Tested whether Pass 267's six-investigator list was already the original field delegation; contemporary press contradicts that simplification.
Did not treat Choi Ju-il's absence from the May 9 report as proof he resigned or was removed.
Did not treat Kim Gwang-jun and Jo Jeong-hun's May 9 presence as proof of the date/mechanism of their appointment.
Separated a planned Interior Committee field team reported in press from the later report-signing special committee.
Used constituency/Hanja evidence to reduce namesake risk rather than matching names alone.
Preserved Lee Seok-gi's birth-date conflict rather than choosing the more precise-looking date.
Treated FRUS's Article 49 characterization as corroboration, not a replacement for Korean stenographic/legal originals.
Treated the NIHK constitutional-history synthesis as a locator for Record No.57, not as the primary record itself.
Did not infer guilt, innocence, neutrality or partisan motive from committee membership.
Did not infer Choi Ju-il's 1948 election outcome from appearance in a UNTCOK candidate list.
